name: Shelly 1PM Gen4 (EU)

radios.note: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee. Matter over Wi-Fi is the default firmware; Zigbee is an alternative mode you switch to.

matter.note: CSA lists Shelly 1PM Gen4 (CSA250D4MAT45094-24, Matter 1.3, firmware 1.3.0-s2, Wi-Fi). A separate CSA entry covers Zigbee.

apple_home.note: Through Matter in the default firmware. Needs an Apple home hub for remote use and automations.

google_home.note: Through Matter. Shelly's page also says it integrates with Google, without saying how, so only Matter is claimed.

alexa.note: Through Matter. Shelly's page also names Alexa; the route is not stated, so only Matter is claimed.

smartthings.note: Through Matter. Shelly's page also names SmartThings; the route is not stated.

home_assistant.note: Official Shelly integration with local push, covering all Shelly generations. It can also be added through Matter.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi device that pairs through Matter or the Shelly app. Zigbee mode needs a Zigbee coordinator, but the default mode does not.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's Shelly integration uses local push; Shelly's page lists scripting, MQTT and webhooks.

switchForm.note: 37 x 42 x 16 mm relay that sits behind an existing switch or socket.

dimmer.note: On/off relay with power metering, 16 A at 240 V AC.

neutralRequired.note: Shelly's spec lists 'Neutral not needed: No'; the AC wiring uses L and N terminals.

gangs.note: Single relay output with one switch input.

summary: The Shelly 1PM Gen4 is a 16 A relay module with power metering that hides behind an existing switch or socket. It ships with Matter over Wi-Fi and is CSA-certified, so Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings can add it without a hub. Home Assistant's Shelly integration controls it locally. It needs a neutral wire.
caveats: Needs a neutral wire at the box; it cannot be installed on a live-only switch loop.
Zigbee is an alternative firmware mode you switch to; Matter is the default. Community reports say input state is not exposed over Zigbee.
Power measurement is not available when the module runs on 24-30 V DC.
Apple Home needs a home hub for remote control and automations.
